# 7. Errors, conditions and restarts

<!-- Generated by tools/generate-docs.lisp from docs/manual/chapters.lisp,
     docs/manual/introduction.md and the examples: do not edit by hand. -->

Errors are conditions that handlers catch; restarts let a handler choose how to
go on without unwinding first.

## Signalling and catching errors

`examples/conditions-basics.lisp`:

```scheme
; error makes a condition from a message and irritants; guard catches it.
(define (checked-sqrt x)
  (if (< x 0)
      (error "checked-sqrt: negative argument:" x)
      [x sqrt]))

(display (guard (e ((error-object? e)
                    (list (error-object-message e) (error-object-irritants e))))
  (checked-sqrt -4)))
(newline)
(display (guard (e ((error-object? e) (condition-report e)))
  (checked-sqrt -9)))
(newline)
(display (checked-sqrt 16))                       ; nothing raised: the body's value
(newline)

; Any value can be raised, and the clauses pick by what it is.
(define (classify-raise thunk)
  (guard (e ((symbol? e) (list 'symbol e))
            ((pair? e) (list 'list (car e)))
            ((string? e) (list 'string e))
            (else (list 'other e)))
    (thunk)))
(display (map classify-raise
              (list (lambda () (raise 'out-of-paper))
                    (lambda () (raise (list 'jammed 3)))
                    (lambda () (raise "on fire"))
                    (lambda () (raise 42)))))
(newline)

; Errors from primitives and from Smalltalk are conditions too.
(define (try thunk)
  (guard (e ((error-object? e) (error-object-message e)))
    (thunk)))
(display (try (lambda () (car 5))))
(newline)
(display (try (lambda () (/ 1 0))))
(newline)
(display (try (lambda () [42 frobnicate])))
(newline)

; With no matching clause, the condition goes on to an outer guard.
(display (guard (outer (#t (list 'outer-caught outer)))
  (guard (inner ((string? inner) 'inner-caught))
    (raise 'not-a-string))))
(newline)

; => passes the test's value to a procedure, as in cond.
(display (guard (e ((assq 'code (if (pair? e) e '())) => cdr))
  (raise (list (cons 'code 404) (cons 'reason "not found")))))
(newline)
```

Its output:

```text
(checked-sqrt: negative argument: (-4))
checked-sqrt: negative argument: -9
4
((symbol out-of-paper) (list jammed) (string on fire) (other 42))
car: not a pair: 5
division by zero
42 does not understand #frobnicate
(outer-caught not-a-string)
404
```

## Handlers that run before unwinding

`examples/conditions-handlers.lisp`:

```scheme
; raise-continuable asks a handler for a value and carries on with it.
(define (lookup key table)
  (let ((entry (assq key table)))
    (if entry
        (cdr entry)
        (raise-continuable (list 'missing key)))))

(define table '((a . 1) (b . 2)))
(display (with-exception-handler
           (lambda (c) 0)                         ; a default for anything missing
           (lambda () (+ (lookup 'a table) (lookup 'b table) (lookup 'z table)))))
(newline)

; The handler sees the condition while the computation is still there: here it
; logs every missing key and supplies a different default each time.
(define seen '())
(display (with-exception-handler
           (lambda (c)
             (set! seen (cons (car (cdr c)) seen))
             (* 100 (length seen)))
           (lambda () (list (lookup 'x table) (lookup 'a table) (lookup 'y table)))))
(newline)
(display (reverse seen))
(newline)

; dynamic-wind's after runs however the thunk is left: normally, or by an error
; unwinding to a guard (after runs before the guard's clause).
(define trail '())
(define (note x) (set! trail (cons x trail)))
(define (guarded thunk)
  (guard (e (#t (note 'handled) 'recovered))
    (dynamic-wind
      (lambda () (note 'enter))
      thunk
      (lambda () (note 'exit)))))
(display (guarded (lambda () (note 'work) 'done)))
(newline)
(display (guarded (lambda () (note 'work) (error "failed"))))
(newline)
(display (reverse trail))
(newline)

; Returning from a handler of a plain raise is itself an error.
(display (guard (e ((error-object? e) (error-object-message e)))
  (with-exception-handler (lambda (c) 'ignored) (lambda () (raise 'stop)))))
(newline)
```

Its output:

```text
3
(100 1 200)
(x y)
done
recovered
(enter work exit enter work exit handled)
handler returned from a non-continuable raise
```

## Recovering without unwinding first

`examples/restarts.lisp`:

```scheme
; A low-level parser finds bad input and offers ways to go on; it does not decide.
(define (parse-entry s)
  (let ((n [s asInteger]))
    (if (smalltalk-nil? n)
        (restart-case (error "not a number:" s)
          (use-value (v) v)                         ; use this value instead
          (skip () 'skip))                          ; leave the entry out
        n)))

(define (parse-all strings)
  (let loop ((ss strings) (acc '()))
    (if (null? ss)
        (reverse acc)
        (let ((v (parse-entry (car ss))))
          (loop (cdr ss) (if (eq? v 'skip) acc (cons v acc)))))))

(define input '("10" "twenty" "30" "forty"))

; Callers higher up choose the recovery, from a handler, before anything unwinds.
(display (with-exception-handler (lambda (c) (invoke-restart 'skip))
           (lambda () (parse-all input))))
(newline)
(display (with-exception-handler (lambda (c) (use-value 0))
           (lambda () (parse-all input))))
(newline)
(display (with-exception-handler
           (lambda (c) (use-value [(car (error-object-irritants c)) size]))
           (lambda () (parse-all input))))             ; the length of the bad text
(newline)

; Handlers can look at what is on offer.
(display (with-exception-handler
           (lambda (c) (use-value (map restart-name (compute-restarts))))
           (lambda () (parse-entry "x"))))
(newline)

; An unbound variable offers use-value and store-value.
(display (with-exception-handler (lambda (c) (use-value 1))
           (lambda () (+ not-yet-defined 41))))
(newline)
(display (with-exception-handler (lambda (c) (store-value 100))
           (lambda () (* not-yet-defined-either 2))))
(newline)
(display not-yet-defined-either)                       ; store-value defined it
(newline)

; Invoking a restart that is not active is an error.
(display (guard (e ((error-object? e) (error-object-message e)))
  (invoke-restart 'skip)))
(newline)
```

Its output:

```text
(10 30)
(10 0 30 0)
(10 6 30 5)
(use-value skip abort)
42
200
100
invoke-restart: no active restart named skip
```
